To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electric charge of a plastic particle in a triboelectric separator can be calculated as a sum of two components, one due to the tribocharging and another one due to the corona charging, and that the critical velocity of the plastic particles can be determined as the ratio of the electric field strength to the particle mass.
the electric charge of plastic particles increases linearly with their velocity in the range of 0.1–1 m s-1.

(i) the electric charge of plastic particles in the triboelectric separator can be estimated from the electric field intensity at the position of the particle, (ii) the critical velocity of plastic particle can be estimated from a combination of electric field and particle mass, and (iii) both of the aforementioned parameters can be estimated from simple equations, without any need for numerical simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the triboelectric separation technique, which is based on a simple, low-cost, and environmentally friendly process.
the triboelectric separation process of plastic particles in a high voltage electric field.
the following: the estimation of charges of plastic particles, their critical velocity, and the influence of the particle shape on the critical velocity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the triboelectric separation is a very effective method for the separation of plastic particles of different densities.
the electric charges on plastic particles are not uniformly distributed, but that their magnitude is a function of the particle size.

the distribution of charges is determined by the properties of particles and by their contact with the triboelectric separator, while the critical velocity depends on the properties of particles, on the applied electric field and on the properties of the separator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electric charge distribution of particles is a function of their size, shape, material, and surface condition and it is independent of the separation process.

triboelectric separation can be successfully applied to the separation of plastic particles, but that the separation efficiency depends strongly on the applied voltage and the particle size and shape, and that the separation efficiency can be improved by increasing the applied voltage, decreasing the particle size and/or increasing their shape factor.
the distribution of electric charges is not significantly affected by the applied electric fields, but the critical velocity of particles increases linearly with the electric field strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical velocity can be estimated from a single experiment and it is independent of particle size and shape.

the distribution of charges on plastic particles can be estimated by the use of a simple model based on the assumption of the existence of a single charge transfer process between the particle and the surface of the triboelectric separator, and the critical velocity of plastic can be estimated by a simple model based only on the particle mass, the electric field intensity at the separator surface, and the electric field gradient in the separator.
the critical velocities of particles with different electric charges are not significantly different.
